articles.title: IND vs NZ 4th ODI | 'Pace is good, but skills matter': Auqib Nabi on adapting to New Zealand conditions
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India pacer Auqib Nabi believes that having pace is an advantage, but trusting one's skills is equally important.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India pacer Auqib Nabi believes that having pace is an advantage, but trusting one's skills is equally important. The Jammu and Kashmir pacer says he will stick to the methods that brought him success in domestic cricket as he prepares for the fourth ODI against New Zealand.Nabi had a quiet start to the five-match series, returning figures of 0/33 in the first ODI, which India won by five wickets (DLS method).He bounced back in the second match, dismissing New Zealand openers Will Young and Tim Seifert to help India register a four-run victory (DLS method).The third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned due to rain, with India leading the series 2-0. The fourth match will be played at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday."Having pace is good but I back my skills. I will do what I have been doing and what has brought me here. I will just do what I did in domestic cricket, and that will help me here too," Nabi said during the press conference ahead of the fourth ODI.Learning to bowl in New Zealand conditionsPlaying his first series in New Zealand, Nabi knows that he will need to adapt to the conditions. The pacer believes that seam movement will be important, as batters can deal with swing bowling."It is my first time in New Zealand. You need to rely more on seam here. Use scrambled seam because swing can be dealt with," he said.Nabi also highlighted the importance of bowling with discipline, particularly on good batting pitches where bowlers can easily leak runs."You need to bowl well no matter how good or flat the pitches are. When wickets are good, you need to bowl with discipline because you can go for runs," he said."We keep discussing amongst ourselves about plans for drop-in pitches. With Arshdeep and Anshul both," he said."Weather back home and here is similar. Opposition and level of cricket is different," he said.From Ranji Trophy success to India coloursKnown as the 'Baramulla Express', Nabi earned his place in the Indian team through consistent performances in domestic cricket.The Jammu and Kashmir pacer picked up 104 wickets across the 2024-25 and 2025-26 Ranji Trophy seasons. His standout performance came in the 2025-26 season, when he picked 60 wickets in 17 innings at an average of 12.65. His efforts played a key role in Jammu and Kashmir winning their maiden Ranji Trophy title. He was also named Player of the Tournament.Nabi admitted that he had expected a Test call-up before getting an opportunity in white-ball cricket. However, he believes the current experience will help him when he gets another chance in the red-ball format."I was expecting a red-ball call-up before white-ball cricket, but this experience will also be very helpful. And then also staying with the Test team," he said."Very happy to play for India. Khelna India ke liye bahut badi baat hai. Mera bhi wohi tha," he added."Whenever people say about facilities, I always say do your best and things will fall in place," the pacer said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IPL: Hardik Pandya, Arshdeep Singh swap jerseys
articles.summary: MUMBAI: In one of the biggest trades in IPL history, Mumbai Indians (MI) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) have swapped two of India's premier white-ball players,
articles.body: MUMBAI: In one of the biggest trades in IPL history, Mumbai Indians (MI) and Punjab Kings (PBKS) have swapped two of India's premier white-ball players, with Hardik Pandya moving to Punjab and Arshdeep Singh heading to Mumbai.Pandya, who captained MI over the last three seasons but could not restore the franchise to its title-winning ways, will begin a new chapter with PBKS. The IPL confirmed on Wednesday that Pandya will join Punjab for Rs 18 crore, up from his previous fee of Rs 16.35 crore, while Arshdeep moves to MI on his existing Rs 18-crore contract.Pandya had attracted interest from multiple franchises, with Kolkata Knight Riders and Rajasthan Royals understood to have explored a deal. However, PBKS succeeded in landing the India all-rounder by parting with their premier fast bowler in what is arguably the most significant trade ahead of the league's 20th edition.The move reflects the differing priorities of the two franchises. Punjab, still chasing their maiden IPL title, have acquired an experienced match-winner and proven leader, while MI have secured one of the world's best left-arm pacers to bolster their bowling attack.While Pandya has harboured captaincy ambitions at the international level and franchise level, he swiftly put to rest any speculation over Punjab's leadership structure, making it clear that he would play under captain Shreyas Iyer. Posting a picture in PBKS colours on Instagram, he wrote: "Sat Sri Akal. My captain, Shreyas. My coach, Ricky. My team, all of Punjab. I am standing behind you."For MI, Arshdeep's arrival fills a long-standing gap. Partnering Jasprit Bumrah, India's talismanic fast bowler now has an equally accomplished left-arm counterpart alongside him. Arshdeep's ability to swing the new ball and execute yorkers at the death gives Mumbai a varied and potent pace attack.Arshdeep leaves PBKS after eight seasons with the franchise, during which he became their highest wicket-taker with 111 wickets in 96 matches. His IPL exploits paved the way for international success, and he currently stands as India's leading wicket-taker in T20Is with 151 wickets in 104 matches."Arshdeep's arrival adds an exciting dimension to our bowling attack," MI owner Akash Ambani said. "He brings the right blend of experience, skill and hunger to compete."Punjab, meanwhile, paid an emotional tribute to their departing stalwart, posting on social media: "From a young sher to a name that made Punjab proud. You'll always have a home here, Arsh paa."The trade also brings the curtain down on Pandya's eventful association with MI. He was a key member of their title-winning sides in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020 before leading Gujarat Titans to the IPL crown in 2022 and another final in 2023. He returned to Mumbai as captain in 2024, replacing Rohit Sharma, but endured mixed fortunes.Under Pandya, MI finished last in 2024, reached the playoffs in 2025 and ended ninth in 2026. His record as captain read 15 wins and 24 defeats in 39 matches."Hardik has shared some very special moments with MI," Ambani said. "We have seen him grow as a cricketer, make his mark on the world stage and then return to lead the team. We wish him nothing but the very best."TOI understands that PBKS skipper Iyer played a significant role in convincing Pandya to make the move. While Punjab gain a proven all-rounder, a power hitter and finisher and leadership option, MI embark on a new era under head coach Kieron Pollard, with Robin Uthappa, Mitchell McClenaghan and T Dilip joining the support staff ahead of IPL 2027.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We absolutely support Pat': Cricket Australia backs Cummins amid fresh Sandpapergate row
articles.summary: Cricket Australia chairman David Boon has thrown his support behind Test captain Pat Cummins following fresh allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering
articles.body: Cricket Australia chairman David Boon has thrown his support behind Test captain Pat Cummins following fresh allegations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Boon has made it clear that Cummins' position as captain is safe and that the board continues to have full faith in him.The controversy has returned to the spotlight after former Australia batter Usman Khawaja made fresh claims in his autobiography, "Sabr". Khawaja alleged that all members of the Australian team on the 2018 South Africa tour knew about the plan to tamper with the ball.His claims have reopened the debate over the scandal and led to demands for another investigation. Cummins, who now leads Australia's Test team, has also come under pressure to explain what he knew.Boon says Cricket Australia has full faith in CumminsBoon said Cummins had led the team with honesty and had the board's complete backing.“We absolutely support Pat,” Boon said in comments published by The Australian on Thursday.“He’s been an exemplary captain, he’s led the team with integrity and, you know, very successfully over the period of time that he’s been captain, so there’s no question of our confidence in him continuing on in that fact.”Cummins has not yet publicly addressed Khawaja's allegations. He, however, posted on X that he would speak to the media on Friday after going through the claims."I've taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy's allegations so I can respond properly," he wrote.Mitchell Marsh, Australia's white-ball captain, is also expected to address the issue. Marsh was part of the Test team during the 2018 tour and will speak at a press conference in Perth later on Thursday, ahead of the ODI against England.Warner and Sayers support Khawaja's versionKhawaja's claims have received support from former teammate David Warner. Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were all banned for their roles in the ball-tampering scandal.Former Australia fast bowler Chadd Sayers, who was also part of the 2018 South Africa tour, has also backed Khawaja. Speaking to Australian media last weekend, Sayers said the allegations were "accurate".Despite the fresh claims, Cricket Australia CEO Todd Greenberg said on Tuesday that there was no compelling reason to reopen the investigation.Boon repeated the same position, saying the board did not want to get into a dispute over different versions of events."I respect (Usman’s) point of view and his recollections of what occurred, and they’re his, but we don’t want to get into a he-said-she-said argument," he said."There are going to be supporters, there’s going to be other guys that don’t recollect the same thing, so I don’t see a purpose.”Hick and Starc deny prior knowledgeIn his book "Sabr", released this week, Khawaja claimed that Australia had tampered with the ball during the second Test in South Africa as well, and not just in the third Test in Cape Town.Former Australia batting coach Graeme Hick has strongly rejected the claims, calling them "absolutely false"."In regard to any discussions around the ball-tampering in Port Elizabeth or Cape Town that took place, I will say in true honesty that I did not hear or know anything," he told the Sydney Morning Herald.Fast bowler Mitchell Starc has also denied having prior knowledge of the ball-tampering.In 2021, Starc and fellow bowlers Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon issued a joint statement. They said they did not know that a "foreign substance" had been taken onto the field to tamper with the ball during the Cape Town Test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India contemplate releasing Gurnoor Brar early for Test preparations
articles.summary: Mount Maunganui: The Indian team management is contemplating releasing Gurnoor Brar from the ODI squad.
articles.body: Mount Maunganui: The Indian team management is contemplating releasing Gurnoor Brar from the ODI squad. TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Brar could be released after the fourth ODI, with a final decision expected after Friday's fixture in Tauranga.With New Zealand having tall bowlers in their squad, the management is keen to have Brar with the Test squad in Wellington. The fast bowler is not part of the India Test squad but has been asked to stay back.India's batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed that the support staff would split after the Hamilton ODI. Head coach Gautam Gambhir and spin bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule are with the ODI set-up, while Kotak, bowling coach Morne Morkel and fielding coach Subhadeep Ghosh are accompanying the Test squad.Gill, KL Rahul and Anshul Kamboj left Hamilton for Wellington, while the remaining players, who are part of the India A set-up, joined the group from Christchurch.Ruturaj Gaikwad likely to openAs far as the fourth ODI against New Zealand is concerned, India are likely to make two changes, with Ruturaj Gaikwad coming in as an opener in place of Shubman Gill, while Ishan Kishan is expected to retain his place in the middle order.A late shake-up cannot be ruled out, but cues from the nets and discussions within the group point to Kishan batting in the middle order for the remaining two ODIs.All the batters, including Tilak Varma, had extended batting sessions in the nets. Ruturaj looked assured and will be keen to make the most of the opportunities in the series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Australia, England set for ODI series opener in Perth
articles.summary: Perth: Australia and England will renew their historic rivalry when they face off in the opening match of a three-match ODI series at Perth Stadium on
articles.body: Perth: Australia and England will renew their historic rivalry when they face off in the opening match of a three-match ODI series at Perth Stadium on Friday.Ahead of the series opener, Australia captain Mitchell Marsh and his England counterpart Harry Brook took part in a pre-series trophy unveiling ceremony in Perth. The two captains also shared a cup of tea at a specially arranged table at the venue, in a light-hearted build-up to the contest.The unique activity celebrated the rich cricketing heritage shared by the two nations, which were among the pioneers of international cricket.The opening ODI, a day-night fixture, will begin at 11.30 am local time. The second match will be played at Adelaide Oval on November 15, before the series concludes at Hobart's Bellerive Oval on November 18.The teams will then switch to the shortest format for a five-match T20I series, beginning at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on November 21.The T20I series will also travel to Gold Coast, Brisbane and Sydney before concluding at Manuka Oval in Canberra on December 2.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Virat Kohli and the art of not ceding an inch
articles.summary: TimesofIndia.com in Mount Maunganui: Virat Kohli on Thursday meant business when the team assembled for training ahead of the fourth ODI against New
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Mount Maunganui: Virat Kohli on Thursday meant business when the team assembled for training ahead of the fourth ODI against New Zealand. From the moment he entered the covered nets area, the ODI stalwart was unusually chirpy as he faced the trio of Gurnoor Brar, Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh. Speaking fluent Punjabi, he questioned the fielding setup and gave feedback on bowling lengths to Brar and Arshdeep.Arshdeep, in particular, had an eventful contest with Kohli; the two were at it for close to twenty minutes. What started as friendly banter quickly turned into a fiery duel after the left-arm seamer cleaned up Kohli, leaving him in disbelief. Disgruntled, Kohli marched to the other end, making way for Rohit Sharma. Even while waiting for his turn, he kept thinking about the dismissal and punched his gloves together in frustration. The signal was clear: bring it on!One could sense the energy Kohli was riding after the blip, and he charged the first Arshdeep delivery he faced only to slice thin air. The bowler, too, kept playing along, finishing his follow-through next to the batter with his hands resting behind his head. The jibes continued in Punjabi but only lasted a few deliveries before Kohli moved to the net where the spinners Axar Patel, Naman Dhir and Kuldeep Yadav were operating. He was out of the firing line but kept needling Arshdeep after animated appeals."Hain? Howzat?" he would jokingly ask, even making a DRS gesture, when Arshdeep appealed during his spell. The youngster did have the last laugh, but Kohli wasn't done competing, and certainly not chatting.Round 2 happened with Kuldeep when the chinaman made the right-hander play one back to his stumps. As Kuldeep celebrated, Kohli played it down: “Ye koi ball thi wicket ki?," he said before deciding to pause.Arshdeep kept talking about length and mindset with Kohli, who shared his experience with the bowlers. He narrated an instance of facing a quick Jofra Archer delivery in the IPL that rose sharply from the good-length spot, stressing the importance of lengths, while assessing the pitch.It was a long hit for Kohli on Thursday. He faced a mix of fast bowling, spin and throwdowns, but he brought match-like energy, making it a very lively session for the squad. There was the occasional chatter with head coach Gautam Gambhir and plenty of laughs, but what stood out was his unwillingness to give an inch.No matter what he did or who he faced, Kohli simulated match-like energy in the semi-closed setting and didn't leave the facility without ticking off his required boxes. Right from the football session with Brar to his cool-down chat with stand-in skipper Shreyas Iyer, Kohli's afternoon had purpose written all over it. As he walked back, the fans wanted a piece of the Indian superstar.Patiently, he signed whatever came his way and called it a day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Can't really target anyone individually': Tim Seifert explains why India's bowling attack has troubled New Zealand
articles.summary: New Zealand's batters have found little room to breathe against India's disciplined pace attack, and Tim Seifert believes the biggest challenge has been
articles.body: New Zealand's batters have found little room to breathe against India's disciplined pace attack, and Tim Seifert believes the biggest challenge has been the visitors' ability to operate as a unit rather than rely on one standout bowler.With India leading the five-match ODI series 2-0, the New Zealand wicketkeeper-batter admitted his side could not identify a particular Indian bowler to target, crediting the variety and consistency within the attack for putting the hosts under pressure.India's pace battery, featuring Arshdeep Singh, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi and Gurnoor Brar, has troubled New Zealand in the first two matches. Gurnoor has emerged as the leading wicket-taker in the series with seven scalps, while the third ODI in Hamilton was abandoned without a ball being bowled due to rain.'They work well as a unit': Seifert on India's pace attackSeifert pointed to the different qualities each Indian pacer brings to the attack, particularly highlighting the advantage of having a left-arm option in Arshdeep."They all bowl very well, they all do something slightly different. Having Arshdeep (Singh) as a left-hander, I think it's crucial as well. But to be honest, they work well as a unit. They all do something a little bit different," Seifert said during the pre-match press conference."To their credit, they didn't miss much on those wickets the last two games. I can't really target anyone individually; I think they do a very good job together," he added.New Zealand looking to regroup after 2-0 deficitDespite the results not going their way, Seifert said New Zealand had faced challenging batting conditions and were focused on making the most of the remaining two matches. The hosts have also undergone changes in personnel, with several players leaving the ODI squad to prepare for the upcoming Test series, which begins on November 19."It's good. I think, look, obviously the result hasn't necessarily gone our way, but we've obviously been put in some tricky situations with the wickets as well. So, look, it's a new bunch of guys here. A few guys have left for the Test series starting on November 19, so we're just focusing on the next two games ahead," he said.Seifert unfazed by changes in personnelAsked about the changes in personnel in both camps, Seifert said the challenge remained the same regardless of who featured in the playing XI. He insisted that every player coming into the side would be an international cricketer capable of making an impact, adding that New Zealand would approach the final two matches with the same competitive mindset."No matter who India play or whoever we play as well, we're out there for the challenge, and everyone's an international cricketer out there. So whoever steps into their role, they're going to try their best. Same with us, whoever steps into the role that the boys have left, everyone's going to try their best as well," he concluded.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
